title: 14. I Won't Play with You!
reviewMethod: English read-aloud translation compared with every original Korean page

pages.text: Bori and Kongi were always together. Side by side on the slide, side by side on the swings, and skipping hand in hand. We're the very best of friends! They looked at each other and giggled.
During free play, Hori called Kongi. Kongi, let's build with blocks! Kongi ran over excitedly. Left alone, Bori pouted and felt a little hurt inside.

When the game ended, Kongi returned. Bori, let's play now! But Bori turned away. Hmph! You left me behind. I won't play with you! What? Then I won't play with you, either! Hmph! They turned their backs on each other.
Bori went down the slide alone. Whoosh! But it wasn't any fun. Far away, Kongi swung alone, stopping and starting with a creak. Being alone isn't any fun.
It was snack time, with their favorite strawberry milk! Bori sipped alone in one corner, and Kongi sipped alone in another. It had tasted better when they shared. Being alone isn't any fun.
At drawing time, Bori used a blue pencil, and Kongi used a yellow one. But there was no partner to ask, Isn't it pretty? Without a friend to show, drawing felt dull. Being alone isn't any fun.

On the yellow bus home, they usually sat together. Today Bori sat alone in front, and Kongi sat alone in back, both staring out of the window. The bus rumbled on, but their hearts felt empty. Being alone isn't any fun.
Bori kept thinking about Kongi. Kongi kept thinking about Bori. Was I the one who got upset first? Was I the one who got angry first? Both felt a little sting in their noses.
The next morning, they met outside preschool. Bori ran over first. Kongi, I'm sorry about yesterday. Tears filled Kongi's eyes, too. I'm sorry, too! I missed you so much! They hugged tightly.

They stayed together all day, on the slide, at snack time, and on the bus. The same games were a hundred times more fun with a friend. Friends can quarrel and still be friends. With a little sorry, we can be close again.
